stage1.impression: Through-the-window night view into a deep, timber-lined bar. The depth, the record wall and the blackened-steel mullions have real atmosphere, but the frame is underexposed and mostly crushed. The etched name reads as an opaque pink-beige decal, cut off at the left edge. The far altar, where the speakers should be the hero, is a murky brown smudge. The glass carries no reflections, so it reads as no glass at all. As it stands it is a competent moody render of a generic dark bar, not yet a specific place a magazine would run.

blocking_9: The EARF pair on the altar must read at a glance as the hero: region [320,230,440,290] lum_median >= 45, with their smoked acrylic and horn visibly lit
Frame lum_median between 22 and 40 (now 14.6), with the bottom sill band [0,420,470,480] crush_pct < 50 and holding steel texture
The etched name must read as a frosted etch in glass (translucent, fine-grained, catching light at its edges) rather than an opaque painted decal, and it must be fully in frame
The shopfront glass must show faint, believable reflections (the street lamps, the kerb) so the camera clearly sits outside behind glass
The frosted lightbox with the dancer's silhouette (named on the card) must be in frame and readable; it is not legible now
No bare, neutral-white hot spot in the room: the source at [395,140,412,158] clips 37 % and is cooler than every other source
The pavement slab [520,450,720,480] must read as real worn concrete, not a flat beige plane

defects.what: The etched name 'EARF' reads as an opaque matte pink-beige vinyl decal (lum_median 60, flat fill). It has no etch grain or edge glow, and the 'E' is cut off by the frame edge
The altar speakers are near-invisible dark shapes (lum_median 21.5, p95 55). The hero product is not read
A bare, near-neutral white disc (RGB ~195/188/184, 37 % clipped) floats mid-room. Every other source is warm. It reads as a CG point lamp or a stray reflection
The sill and stall-riser band is crushed (crush_pct 20.5, lum_median 5.8). The steel there is a black void
The central steel mullion is very dark (lum_median 10). Its patina shows only in the upper part; the lower 2/3 is flat
The pavement reads as a flat, evenly lit beige plane (lum_median 121, low texture) with a hard CG edge. It is brighter than anything inside the room
A pale frosted panel (presumably the lightbox) is seen obliquely through the side bay. No dancer silhouette is legible, and the panel reads as a blank pink rectangle
The side bay is a plain beige wall with a sheer curtain, unrelated to the main room. It reads as a different, empty space and splits the composition
There are no reflections on the shopfront glass anywhere, so the window reads as an open hole
Ceiling and beams are dim and uniformly red-brown (r 27 / g 10 / b 4 median). The grade is over-saturated orange in the shadows, with little neutral concrete
The table lamp/Orb on the front table is a small blown blob (0.8 % clip) on an otherwise empty table. It reads as a placeholder

changes.problem: The hero speakers on the altar are lost in the murk at the end of the room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 21.5, p95 55.3; speakers read only as dark silhouettes

change.to: 260 W, 2500 K, cone 24 deg, aimed at each speaker's horn and upper cabinet so the smoked acrylic glows

changes.expected: The pair becomes the brightest coloured object at the vanishing point, with readable horn mouths and lit acrylic edges

changes.problem: The whole frame is underexposed below the brief's night-interior range.
changes.expected: Frame median about 24-30; the room's shadows hold detail while the lamps stay unclipped

changes.problem: The etched name is cropped at the left edge, and the lightbox with the dancer (a subject the card names) is only a sliver in the side bay.

evidence.measured: the 'E' is cut by the frame edge; the lightbox panel [560,135,590,250] is seen edge-on with no silhouette

change.to: [-4.6, 2.6, 1.5], 28 mm, still level and aimed at [17.0, 3.4, 1.35], so the full name, both mullions and the lightbox face sit inside the frame

changes.expected: The whole shopfront reads as a composed facade: name, door bay, lightbox and the deep room behind

changes.problem: The etched name reads as opaque painted vinyl rather than frosted etch in glass.

evidence.measured: lum_median 59.9 with flat fill, RGB 81/55/42; no grain, no edge highlight

change.setting: the window's etched name (emission and etch finish)
change.to: emission 0.0, lower the etch's opacity to about 40 % transmission-frost with a fine roughness, so the room shows through and the edges catch the street light

changes.expected: The letters read as pale, translucent frost about 25-40 lum over the room, with the record wall faintly visible through them

changes.problem: The steel shopfront is a black void at the bottom, and the glass carries no reflections, so the camera does not read as being outside behind glass.

change.to: keep two at 90 W; move one to about 1.5 m left of camera at 3 m high and raise it to 160 W, so it grazes the steel at a low angle and leaves a soft streak reflection on the glass

changes.expected: The sill and mullion patina become readable (brownish, uneven sheen); a faint warm street-lamp reflection appears on the glass

changes.problem: A cool, near-white clipped disc floats in the middle of the room and breaks the single warm light family.

evidence.measured: RGB median 195/188/184, clip_pct 37.3, against 2400-2600 K everywhere else

change.setting: the Dome pendant's liner glow (or the source producing the disc)
change.to: glow 0.6 with the smoked tint visible; if it is a street-lamp reflection, move that lamp out of the glass's mirror angle

changes.expected: A warm, smoked glow with no clipping, matching the other pendants

changes.problem: The pavement in the right foreground is a flat, evenly lit beige plane, brighter than anything in the room.

change.to: darker, worn, slightly damp concrete (albedo about 0.18, roughness 0.5 with variation, joint lines and staining)

changes.expected: The kerb recedes and frames the window rather than competing with it

changes.problem: The pools of light from the Domes' downlights have no air in them, so the room reads flat and showroom-clean from the street.

evidence.measured: counter lum_median 42.4 with p95 210: hard hot spots, no visible cones

changes.expected: Soft visible cones under the pendants, with the far altar slightly veiled to give the room depth

out_of_scope.request: Give the side bay at [520,130,650,310] a purpose, or relate it to the main room
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront and room layout are fixed by the card; only camera framing can reduce its weight

out_of_scope.request: Show the dancer silhouette in the lightbox more strongly
out_of_scope.why: What the screens and lightbox show is fixed; only their brightness and the camera may change

out_of_scope.request: Add a person or figure inside for a sign of life
out_of_scope.why: Props are limited to small objects; a figure is beyond the card's allowed changes
